project_reference.core_research_question: Derive first-principles limits on optimal agent scaling N* = f(H, q, T) in LLM-based multi-agent systems using statistical mechanics (partition functions, Ising/Potts models, renormalization group).
project_reference.current_focus: Preparing for Phase 4: Ising-Agent Simulation (Monte Carlo validation)

position.last_activity_desc: Verification audit completed — all Phase 1-3 results validated with corrections applied

active_calculations: H = -J Σ_{⟨ij⟩} δ(s_i, s_j) with J > 0 (ferromagnetic)
Free energy: F = U - TS (explains diversity bonus)
q: Number of distinct agent types (1-16)
J: Alignment strength (0.1-10 in k_B=1 units)
intermediate_results: Cataloged 8+ Ising/Potts model applications to agent systems
Identified 4 established physics results for validation
q → Number of distinct agent types (discrete diversity)
N → Agent count (finite-size effects critical for N<100)
Key finding: D_4 (4 diverse) ≈ 16-32 homogeneous agents
Mean-field assumption validated by fully-connected topology
N*(q,T) = (T/2ε) ln[e^{J/2T} + (q-1)e^{-J/2T}] — N* increases with q
Equal-performance diversity multiplier: max ~3× from pure entropy
RG flow equations: dr/dl, du/dl for momentum-shell integration
Gaussian FP: r*=0, u*=0 with y_r=2, y_u=4-d
Wilson-Fisher FP: r*~ε, u*~ε for d<4
Ginzburg criterion: Gi ~ |T-T_c|^{(4-d)/2}, d=4 upper critical dimension
open_questions: How to incorporate complementarity effects into Hamiltonian?
What is the actual T/J ratio in Yang et al.'s agent system?
Can we calibrate ε from Yang's N* data?
How do finite-size corrections modify N* for N < 20 agents?
decisions: Potts model with mean-field theory chosen as framework (2026-03-16)
Coordination cost F_cost = εN² added for finite N* prediction (2026-03-19)
Yang discrepancy documented: pure entropy gives ~3× max, Yang observes 4-8× (2026-03-19)
ε convention corrected: [ε] = [E] since N is dimensionless count (2026-04-03)
N* interpretation corrected: N* increases with q (diverse systems sustain larger populations) (2026-04-03)
approximations: Mean-field approximation: valid for fully-connected topology, O(1/d) corrections for sparse networks
Saddle-point approximation: O(1/N) finite-size errors, breaks down at N < 10
Gaussian fluctuations: valid away from T_c, O(u) near critical point
Epsilon expansion: O(ε²) errors, unreliable for d ≤ 2 (ε ≥ 2)
Scalar φ⁴ theory: valid for q=2 (Ising), q>2 requires vector field theory

convention_lock.coupling_convention: H = -J Σ δ(s_i, s_j), J>0 ferromagnetic

propagated_uncertainties: ε parameter not empirically calibrated — affects N* magnitude but not scaling
T/J ratio estimated from q_c analysis (1.07-1.14), needs direct measurement
Mean-field approximation accuracy unknown for N < 50 — requires MC validation (Phase 4)
